subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-skill user preference sidecars, and if so should the public contract be markdown sidecar, structured `skills.entries.*.config`, or no core support?
rationale: The gap is real in current source, but the fix changes public skill loading and prompt composition rather than repairing an established bug contract.

options.title: Standardize Markdown Sidecar
options.body: Document and load a `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` file with the selected skill, lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, with prompt-version, watcher, sandbox, and security coverage.

options.title: Use Structured Skill Config
options.body: Keep user preferences under `skills.entries.*.config` and require skills or plugins to interpret them, avoiding a new markdown prompt surface but weakening natural-language convention support.

options.title: Decline Core Support
options.body: Keep the current model of full skill overrides, Skill Workshop proposals, or global context files if maintainers do not want another skill-loading surface.

recommendation.title: Standardize Markdown Sidecar
recommendation.body: Document and load a `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` file with the selected skill, lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, with prompt-version, watcher, sandbox, and security coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The freshest checked history and issue timeline point to steipete around grouped skill loading, docs, and product/API decisions for skills.
